title: Methodus generalior numeros quosvis satis grandes perscrutandi utrum sint primi necne?

deep.reconstruction:
This page finishes Euler's primality proof for N = 18518809 = 1848·100² + 197². The method rests on idoneal numbers: 1848 is an idoneal number, so N is prime exactly when its only representation N = 1848x² + y² (with gcd(1848x, y) = 1) is the known one. On earlier pages Euler used congruences to reduce y = 197 + 21z and split the possibilities into four residue cases. Each case becomes an equation of the form 10000 − S(t) = x², where S is a quadratic in t.

Case four (§70) starts from 10000 − ½(3s+197)(77s+5122) = x². Shifting s = t − 66 gives 10000 − ½(3t−1)(77t+40) = x². Taking t of both signs, the subtrahends are S = ½(3t∓1)(77t±40):
- t ≥ 0: S = −20, 117, 485, 1084, … with differences 137, 368, 599, … (second difference 231).
- t ≤ 0: S = −20, 74, 399, 955, … with differences 94, 325, 556, ….

Starting from 10020 = 10000 + 20, Euler subtracts the arithmetically growing differences and stops when the next difference exceeds the remainder.
- Left column: 9883, 9515, 8916, 8086, 7025, 5733, 4210, 2456, 471.
- Right column: 9926, 9601, 9045, 8258, 7240, 5991, 4511, 2800, 858.
None of these is a square.

§71: since no case leaves a square, the representation is unique and 18518809 is prime. Euler adds that squares rarely survive such sieves, so the form 1848a² + b² is very suitable for producing many huge primes by varying a and b. He presents this as partly answering 'Fermat's problem' of finding primes larger than any given number.

§72: while b = 197 is fixed, the subtracted numbers do not depend on a, so the same tables can be reused for other (smaller) values of a. To recover y when a square does occur, he back-substitutes: y = 21z + 197, z = 21s − 394, s = t + 18, so z = ±21t − 16 (upper sign for the first column, lower for the second).
errors: No arithmetical errors found. I checked the substitution 3(t−66)+197 = 3t−1 and 77(t−66)+5122 = 77t+40, all S values, all differences, all subtractions, and the non-squareness of every residue (e.g. 9601 vs 98² = 9604; 2800 vs 53² = 2809; 858 vs 29² = 841). I also checked z = 21(t+18) − 394 = 21t − 16.

Gap: the claim that the form 1848a² + b² will 'easily' give many large primes is heuristic. Each new N still needs its own exhaustive check for a second representation, together with the coprimality and idoneal-number conditions. No density or existence argument is given.

ideas.what: Primality proof of 18518809 by showing it has a unique representation by the idoneal form 1848x² + y²
ideas.modern_name: Euler's idoneal-number (convenient-number) primality criterion / class-group-of-one-class-per-genus test
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1778 onward; the 18518809 example is often cited, e.g. in Dickson's History and Weil's Number Theory)
ideas.where_published: Euler's idoneal-number papers of the 1770s–80s (e.g. E498, E699, E708, E719); discussed by Dickson Vol. I and Weil

ideas.what: Sieving x² = C − S(t) for a quadratic S by subtracting first differences that grow by a constant second difference
ideas.modern_name: Finite-difference scan for representations by a quadratic form (Fermat/Euler difference method)
ideas.where_published: Used throughout the same papers (cf. §59 of the neighbouring text with 840x² + y²)

ideas.what: Remark that varying a and b in 1848a² + b² yields arbitrarily large primes, linked to Fermat's problem of exhibiting primes beyond any bound
ideas.modern_name: Generating large certified primes with special forms

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known conclusion of Euler's proof that 18518809 is prime using the idoneal number 1848, which is widely cited in histories of number theory. The arithmetic is correct and nothing new appears.
transcription_corrections: The '[?]' after '1848aa+bb' can be removed: the image clearly reads '1848aa + bb', consistent with 18518809 = 1848·100² + 197².
In the subtraction table, the line '1754 . . . 1711' at the foot of page 44 is a catchword repeated at the top of page 45. Those are the ninth differences, giving remainders 2456 and 2800.
The 'NEXT PAGE' transcription (pp. 36–37, §§58–60 on 64013 and 999601 = 840·34² + 169²) belongs to a different item or section, not to page 46 of E719.
